about.title: Burbank Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription:
A wet entryway, a broken step, a parking lot light that never got fixed — falls in Burbank rarely happen because someone was careless on their own. They happen because a property owner let a hazard sit. Under California premises liability law, that is the heart of your claim: showing the owner knew about the condition, or reasonably should have, and did nothing to repair it or warn you. That is what lawyers call notice, and it is where most of these cases are won or lost.

Burbank is a city of about 105,000 people inside Los Angeles County, with storefronts, apartment complexes, and office lots spread along corridors like Glenoaks Boulevard. Whether you fell at a grocery store, a rental property, or a city-owned sidewalk, the property type changes your deadline. Most claims carry a two-year window; claims against a public entity move much faster.

We handle premises liability cases on contingency. You pay nothing unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Burbank Fall Victims Choose Us

items.title: Notice is the whole case — and it needs proof fast
items.desc: California requires you to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Our team can move quickly to request surveillance footage before it is overwritten and gather the maintenance records that show how long the problem existed.

items.title: Two deadlines, not one
items.desc: A private-property fall in Burbank generally gives you two years to file, but a claim against a public entity runs on a much shorter clock. Getting us involved early keeps both timelines in view.

items.title: Partial blame does not close the door
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if an insurer argues you were distracted or wearing the wrong shoes, your claim survives and is reduced only by your share of responsibility. We can push back when that share is inflated.

items.question: I fell outside a business on Glenoaks Boulevard in Burbank. What should I do right now?
items.answer: Photograph the exact spot where you fell, including anything that caused it — liquid, a lifted slab, poor lighting — before it gets cleaned up or repaired. Ask the business for an incident report and the names of any employees or shoppers who saw it. Then get medical care the same day, because a gap in treatment is something insurers use against you. Once you have done that, reaching out to us helps preserve any camera footage while it still exists.

items.question: What if I fell on a Burbank city sidewalk or in a public building?
items.answer: Claims involving a public entity in California follow a different and much shorter process than a claim against a private business. You typically must file a formal government claim well before the standard two-year deadline, and missing it can end the case. This is one situation where waiting even a few weeks to contact us can cost you.

items.question: Do you charge me anything, and do you handle my case directly?
items.answer: We handle premises liability cases in the Burbank area on contingency. There is no fee unless your case results in a recovery. Nothing we do promises a particular result; we simply evaluate your situation and represent you directly.
